text: Flag. Do not swim outside the flags.
Warning. A yellow sign is a warning: something is dangerous today.
Patrol. The patrol watches this beach from seven to seven.
Signal. Float, raise one arm and signal to the lifeguards.
Jellyfish. If the water is warm, there will be jellyfish.
Drift. If you stop paddling here, you will drift down the beach.
Sunscreen. Put sunscreen on before you leave the house.
Hazard. The sign says there is a hazard in the water today.
If it's flat tomorrow, I'll go to the gym.
You won't feel it until you're past your waist.
What will you do if the flags are down?
If a rip takes you, don't swim against it.

Right, the report for Tuesday. There is three feet of clean swell on the south coast and the wind is offshore until about ten. If you get down there early, you will have the best two hours of the week. After ten it turns onshore and it will be a mess by lunchtime, so do not plan a long session. One warning for the beaches up north. The patrol is only on from nine, and there is a strong current running along the sandbank at the moment. If you paddle out before nine, nobody will be watching you. If you are not sure, go south.

Hi love, it is me. Quick one before you leave for the beach. There is sunscreen in the blue bag by the door. If you forget it, you will regret it by two o'clock, I promise you. Second thing. The water has been really warm this week, so if you see anything in the water that looks like a plastic bag, get out. That is a jellyfish, and it will hurt for hours. And listen, if the yellow sign is up at the top of the steps, do not go in. Just come home and we will go tomorrow. Text me when you get there.
